data.gender_notes: Aloknath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aloknath is derived from the Sanskrit words 'alok' meaning 'radiant, shining' and 'nath' meaning 'God'. It is a revered name in Hindu tradition, representing the divine presence of a radiant and powerful deity. The name Aloknath carries the meaning “Radiant, Shining God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Aloknath usually hope their child will grow to embody radiant, shining god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_significance: Lord Ganesha is believed to be the remover of obstacles and the god of wisdom, knowledge, and new beginnings. vedic_reference.note: Alokanath is a form of Lord Shiva. He is also known as the 'God of Sight' and the 'Lord of Light'. He is described in various Hindu scriptures, including the Shiva Purana and the Mahabharata.

historical_references.reference: Aloknath is believed to be an ancient name of the Hindu god Vishnu during the Bhagavata Purana period. This name is mentioned when Vishnu appeared to Rishabhdeva in the form of a radiant deity (alokam) to reveal the supreme cosmic truths.

Another reference to Aloknath is found in the 12th century Sanskrit epic 'Mahabharata' where it is used as a name of Arjuna, a central character, during his enlightenment. In this context, Arjuna's spiritual guide Bhagavad Gita reveals divine knowledge to him as Aloknath, the giver of light and wisdom.
